jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/x) Biology (Life Sciences) (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/x) Biology (Life Sciences) for Preclinical ImagingRadiochemie TV-L: 38,5 h/week (100%) 1-year fixed-term contract under the WissZeitVG; plus a 1-year extension for a third-party funded projectYour salary will be based on TV-LYour tasks• Planning, conducting and analyzing the biological evaluation of newly developed PET and SPECT radiotracers• Contributing to the establishment, optimization anddocumentation of biological test systems and preclinical evaluation protocols• Performing in vitro studies, including stability, binding and cellular uptake assays as well as studies using models of the blood-brain-barrier• Preclinical evaluation of tracer candidates in suitable in vivo models, including support of small-animal imaging studies• Performing and analyzing ex vivo studies, e.g., autoradiography, biodistribution studies and complementary tissue analyses• Quantitative analysis of biological and imaging data andinterpretation of results in close interaction with the other project partners• Evaluation, documentation, and scientific presentation of experimental results in project reports, publications, and presentationsYour profile• Completed university degree and Ph.D. in biology, life sciences, neuroscience, biochemistry, pharmacy or a related field• Experience in preclinical imaging (e.g. small animal PET, SPECT, MRI, CT)• Experience with animal models and experimental animal work is advantageous (FELASA-B or EU functions A, C, D)• Experience with cell culture, in vitro assays, autoradiography, ex vivo analyses and BBB models is desirable• Interest in radiopharmaceutical tracer development, molecular imaging and translational research• Willingness to work with unsealed radioactive substances and to become familiar with radiation protection-related workflows• Willingness to conduct biological and preclinical experiments within an interdisciplinary team• Good written and spoken English skills• Structured, independent and conscientious working style• Ability to work in a team, strong communication skills and interest in interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, radiochemistry, biology, medicine and imagingOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future with usWe are one of the leading university hospitals in Germany and network research, teaching and health care at the highest level. That's why many things are a lot bigger for us: the spectrum of exciting development opportunities. The limitless openness with which specialists from all over the world work together here. Or our commitment as an employer to support all employees as best we can in reconciling their job with their goals and life situations.This is the University Hospital of Cologne: Everything but ordinary.Your future in detailThe Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. The postdoc position will initially be embedded for one year in the internationally funded IMAGESTRO project. There is an option of extension for another year. The focus of the work will be on the biological validation of newly developed PET or SPECT radiotracers.The IMAGESTRO project aims to develop novel 18F-labeled PET tracers for the non-invasive imaging of estrogen receptors in the brain, to characterize them preclinically, and to translate them into human applications. The project focuses on the organic synthesis of suitable precursor and reference compounds, the development and optimizationof radiofluorination strategies, and the comprehensive analytical and preclinical characterization of the resulting radiotracers. The work will be carried out in close cooperation between the University Hospital Cologne and Forschungszentrum Jülich and offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of organic chemistry, radiochemistry, radiopharmacy, molecular imaging, biology and neuroscience.Applications from female candidates are expressly welcome and will be given priority in the event of equal suitability, competence and professional performance. People with disabilities are welcome to apply and will be treated preferentially in the event of equal suitability and qualification. The position is suitable for staffing with part-time employees.ContactUniv.-Prof. Dr. Bernd NeumaierTel.: +49 221 478-86807Universitätsklinikum Köln AöRGeschäftsbereich PersonalKerpener Str. 6250937 KölnUniklinik Köln Karriere Application deadline: 13.09.2026Job-ID: 4bxxe1uxWe look forward to receiving your application and getting to know you!

jobs.occupation: Senior Legal Counsel ESG (Jurist/in)
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: OUR COMPANYAt Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.The PositionAre you passionate about shaping the legal framework of sustainability and responsible business practices?As Senior Legal Counsel ESG Law, you will provide highly specialized legal advice on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) matters and support the effective integration of Boehringer Ingelheim's SD4G framework.By translating evolving legal and regulatory requirements into practical guidance, you will enable strategic ESG initiatives across the organization and advise on Social Engagement projects, including those with proximity to venture capital mechanisms.Tasks & responsibilities- Provide strategic legal counsel on ESG-related legal and regulatory requirements, enabling Boehringer Ingelheim to advance its sustainability and social responsibility ambitions in a compliant and future-oriented manner.- Shape the legal interpretation of emerging ESG regulations, including current and upcoming frameworks such as the EU Taxonomy and Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), the EU Empowering Consumers Directive (Green Claims), as well as product compliance related frameworks such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation and translate requirements into actionable business guidance and contractual clauses.- Act as the trusted Legal Business Partner for the Corporate Sustainability team and serve as the central legal contact for the global coordination of SD4G-related matters across Global Legal and Compliance.- Drive the development of pragmatic legal solutions that support reporting obligations, corporate governance requirements, and organizational structures across national and international jurisdictions.- Support impactful sustainability and social engagement initiatives together with the Boehringer Ingelheim Venture Fund legal team by advising on legal risks and opportunities and by structuring, drafting, and negotiating agreements, including transaction, loan, cooperation, and sponsorship contracts.- Represent the Global Legal & Compliance function in relevant committees, steering groups, and external peer networks, fostering collaboration and bringing legal ESG perspectives into strategic discussions.Requirements- Fully qualified lawyer (or equivalent legal qualification), with long-term experience in a leading law firm and/or as in-house counsel in an international environment- Deep expertise in ESG law, including comprehensive knowledge of existing and emerging regulatory frameworks such as the CSRD, and CSDDD- Strong strategic and commercial acumen, ideally gained within the pharmaceutical industry or another highly regulated sector- Proven ability to provide strategic legal advice on ESG matters and to support the implementation of evolving sustainability and social responsibility requirements- Broad experience handling ESG-related legal matters, including contract drafting, review and negotiation, as well as transaction-related agreements and other complex commercial arrangements- Strong analytical and strategic thinking with a long-term focus, able to communicate risk, exercise sound judgment under ambiguity and simplify complex matters for all levels of the organization- Business-oriented mindset and excellent stakeholder management skills in cross-functional and international settings, combined with strong communication skills in EnglishAs part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.comReady to contact us?If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.comRecruitment process:Step 1: Online application - The job posting is presumably online until November 15, 2026. We reserve the right to take the posting offline beforehand.Step 2: Virtual meeting until end of NovemberStep 3: On-site interviews are planned for the beginning of DecemberPlease include the following documents when applying for this position: References (e.g. university degree certificate and employment references)

Operational Strategy Alignment - Support the consolidation of product and domain-level strategies into a coherent operational target picture for Digital Technology. - Work closely with Enterprise Architects, Domain Leads and Product Teams to identify synergies, dependencies and alignment opportunities. - Facilitate cross-domain discussions and help ensure consistent execution against agreed priorities. - Maintain transparency on strategic progress, risks and interdependencies. This includes ensuring that recovery objectives, documentation and governance requirements are understood, maintained and monitored, as well as supporting the identification and resolution of recovery gaps. - Contribute to the further development of resilience capabilities as an increasingly important pillar of Energy Markets Digital Technologies’ operational excellence. jobs.occupation: Postdoc - automated high-throughput screening of electrolyte adduces for aqueous batteries (Ingenieur/in - Materialwissenschaften)
jobs.description: The postdoctoral candidate will work within an international research project focused on improving the performance and long-term stability of aqueous batteries through the development of advanced electrolyte additives.The central objective of the project is to establish an integrated high-throughput workflow combining robotic electrolyte preparation, automated electrochemical testing, and machine-learning-assisted analysis.The work involves extensive experimental laboratory activities, automated testing, electrochemical characterization, data analysis, and close cooperation with industrial project partners. The candidate will contribute to the development of reproducible and data-driven battery research workflows for sustainable, safe, and cost-effective stationary energy-storage technologies.The position is full-time (39 h/week) and fixed-term for 18 months, starting in February 2027.Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position.Your tasks- Develop and optimize automated high-throughput workflows for the preparation and electrochemical screening of aqueous electrolyte formulations.- Systematically screen a broad range of electrolyte additives and generate high-quality datasets linking electrolyte composition to battery performance.- Perform electrochemical characterization using techniques such as galvanostatic cycling, cyclic voltammetry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.- Analyze large experimental datasets and contribute to the development and validation of machine-learning and quantitative structure-property relationship models.- Publish your results in leading peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences, write project reports.- Collaborate closely with researchers, data scientists, and industrial partners working on electrolyte synthesis, battery development, modelling, and scale-up.Your profileRecruitment requirement- A PhD in the subject areas of Materials science, Electrochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or similar.Required knowledge and personal skills- Strong background in electrochemistry and aqueous battery technologies.- Hands-on laboratory experience and interest in experimental research.- Experience with electrochemical measurements and data analysis.- Interest in automated experimentation and data-driven materials research.- Ability to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary research team.- Knowledge of techniques such as EIS, cyclic voltammetry, hydrogen evolution,  and electrode degradation.- Very good English language skills (at least B2/C1 level according to CEFR).Desired knowledge and personal skills- Experience with aqueous batteries, metal-anode batteries, or electrolyte development.- Experience with materials characterization techniques, such as microscopy, X-ray methods.- Experience with automated experimentation, robotics, data science, or machine learning is advantageous.Reach out with your CV and motivation letter expressing your interest and experience in the proposed topic. Got questions before applying? Contact Prof. Zheludkevich (Mikhail.zheludkevich@hereon.de), Dr. Lamaka (Sviatlana.lamaka@hereon.de) or Dr. Snihirova (darya.snihirova@hereon.de).Our offer- Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure- Access to a large international research and industrial network.- Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays- An exciting job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations- International Welcome Office with guest accommodation- 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day- social benefits according to the collective agreement of the public service and remuneration up to EG 13 (according toEntgO Bund)- very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible work- A green campus on the Elbe River, well-connected with Hamburg (public transport), subsidy for the Deutschlandticket if certain conditions are met (job ticket), charging facilities for electric vehicles- family-friendly company policy with childcare facilities, e.g. nursery/kindergarten close to the company- Operational Health Management, e.g. Employee Assistance Program (EAP)- Corporate BenefitsSeverely disabled persons and those equaling severely disabled persons who are equally suitable for the position will be considered preferentially within the framework of legal requirements.Interested? We are looking forward to receiving your application. Karriereseite.

jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.About the position- Salary group 13 TV-L - Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned- 50 % of a full-time position- As soon as possibleThe newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?The role- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)- Thorough documentation of research- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilitiesAbout you- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skillsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 1 November 2026 via our online application portal.Please include the following documents with your application:- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)
